chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the one in Ihraam packing the Dirhams inside his clothes. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes, and he can wear the money-belt and the purse'.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْمِنْطَقَةَ: The money-belt or sash worn around the waist
key_terms.الْهِمْيَانَ: The purse or bag for carrying money
key_terms.يَصُرُّ: To bind, tie, or pack tightly

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihraam to wear a money belt and carry coins in their clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* clarifies the permissibility of wearing a belt (*mintaqah*) and carrying a purse (*himyan*) for pilgrims in *Ihraam*, resolving the distinction between the general prohibition of wearing sewn garments and the allowance for functional accessories. It highlights the practical flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding items necessary for securing wealth during the pilgrimage rites.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one in Ihraam packing the Dirhams inside his clothes. Heasws said: ‘Yes, and he can wear the money-belt and the purse’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who in the state of Ihram keeps dirham in his cloths. He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, he can wear a belt or a purse.’”
